Characteristics — the table:

Accuracy class: (I) and (II) — two columns.

Columns: Class (I): Max ≤ 320 g; e ≥ 0.001 g; n ≤ 320000 divisions.
Class (II): Max ≤ 6200 g, e range 0.1 g ≥ e ≥ 0.01 g, n ≤ 62000 divisions; Max ≤ 12000 g, e ≥ 1 g, n ≤ 12000 divisions.

Hmm, the table structure:
Row 1: Accuracy class | (I) | (II) (colspan 2)
Row 2: Maximum capacity | Max ≤ 320 g | Max ≤ 6200 g | Max ≤ 12000 g
Row 3: Verification scale interval | e ≥ 0,001 g | 0,1 g ≥ e ≥ 0,01 g | e ≥ 1 g
Row 4: Maximum number of scale intervals | n ≤ 320000 divisions | n ≤ 62000 | n ≤ 12000
Row 5: Actual scale interval: e = d or e = 10 d or e = 100 d (colspan 3)
Row 6: Weighing range: Single interval (colspan 3)
Row 7: Tare: T ≤ -Max (colspan 3)
Row 8: Temperature range: +10 °C / +30 °C; +15 °C / +25 °C only for type: AX…5… (class (I)) (colspan 3)
Row 9: Power supply voltage: 12 V DC supplied by AC/DC plug-in power adapter (colspan 3)
Row 10: Software identification: Version number: 1.xx or 2.xx (xx = 00 to 99) (colspan 3)

So this cert covers model variants. The Adventurer AX series with class (I) up to 320 g, and class (II) with max 6200 g or 12000 g. Should these be model_family models? The class columns define different instrument configurations. Possibly model variants: class (I) instrument, class (II) 6200g, class (II) 12000g.

Also there's a type mention: "AX…5…" for class (I) temperature range.

I could model this as model_level matrix with models: "Class I (Max ≤ 320 g)", "Class II (Max ≤ 6200 g)", "Class II (Max ≤ 12000 g)". Or as matrix_tables preserving the table.

Alternatively, use config_level with axis "accuracy_class"? The schema says config axes for configurations like static vs dynamic. Here the variation is by accuracy class column which also implies different Max. I think treating the three columns as model variants is reasonable, similar to R137 example.

Let me define models:
- model_id: "Class I, Max ≤ 320 g"? Better: since it's a family "Adventurer AX series", the models might be AX series variants. But we don't have explicit model numbers except AX…5….

Hmm. Actually the characteristic table defines permitted characteristics by class. The certificate covers the Adventurer AX series. The three columns: class I (max 320g), class II (max 6200g), class II (max 12000g). 

I think the cleanest: model_family with family_name "Adventurer AX series", models:
- {"model_id": "AX (I)", "label": "Accuracy class (I), Max ≤ 320 g", attributes: {...}}
- {"model_id": "AX (II) 6200 g", ...}
- {"model_id": "AX (II) 12000 g", ...}

And model_level characteristics:
- maximum_capacity: values per model: ≤320 g → value {min:null, max:320}, unit g
- verification_scale_interval: class I: {min: 0.001, max: null} g; class II 6200: {min: 0.01, max: 0.1} g; class II 12000: {min:1, max:null} g
- maximum_number_of_scale_intervals: 320000, 62000, 12000 (divisions)
- temperature_range: +10/+30 °C common; +15/+25 only for AX…5… class (I). Could be config_level with axis "model variant AX…5…".

Type-level characteristics:
- actual_scale_interval: "e = d or e = 10 d or e = 100 d" — formula string
- weighing_range: "Single interval"
- tare: "T ≤ -Max" — hmm, negative tare? T ≤ -Max seems odd; usually T = -Max to... whatever, keep string "T ≤ -Max".
- temperature_range: {min:10, max:30} °C; plus special config for AX…5… class (I): {min:15, max:25} °C.
- power_supply_voltage: 12 V; power_supply_type: DC; note "supplied by AC/DC plug-in power adapter".
- software_identification: "Version number: 1.xx or 2.xx (xx = 00 to 99)"

The temperature special: use config_level: attribute temperature_range, axis "instrument_variant", values: [{condition: "type AX…5… (class (I))", value: {min:15, max:25}, unit_symbol "°C"}].

I'll include matrix_tables for the characteristics table preserving it? The schema says matrix_tables for multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. The characteristics table fits into model_level, so maybe not needed. But I could include it for fidelity. I think I'll include it as a matrix_table since it's a 3-column comparison table. Actually, rules say preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. Since model_level covers it, I could skip matrix_tables. But including it doesn't hurt. Hmm — to be safe and complete, I'll include a matrix table "Instrument characteristics by accuracy class" with columns accuracy_class, maximum_capacity, verification_scale_interval, maximum_number_of_scale_intervals. Actually I'll include it, mirroring the R137 example which includes both matrix_tables and model_level.

Footnotes: none present.

Components: none.

Certificate:
- number: "R76/2006-A-NL1-20.56" — revision 1 is separate. Number field: "R76/2006-A-NL1-20.56". Scheme: "A". The number contains "-A-" which indicates scheme A.
- revision: revision_history covers it. Schema certificate doesn't have revision field; fine.
